entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Andrea Alciato (1467-1550) was an Italian jurist and writer, considered the founder of the French school of legal humanists.

As a key figure in the revival of interest in classical Roman law, Alciato's works significantly influenced the development of modern legal theory in Europe.

His treatises on law and politics, particularly 'De Principis Juris', shaped the intellectual landscape of the Renaissance, as thinkers such as Montaigne and Bodin engaged with his ideas.

Alciato's legacy extends to the modern era, with his concepts of 'suum ius' (a person's own law) and 'jurisprudentia' (the science of law) remaining foundational to legal studies.

The French Academy of Legal and Political Sciences, established in 1806, explicitly recognized Alciato as a 'patriarch' of French juridical thought, testifying to the enduring impact of his work.
